problem: Existing quadruped-robot intelligent systems focus on path planning, locomotion control or task-specific policies, or use end-to-end VLA models that depend on specific task distributions and large-scale training data, so they struggle with multitask execution, extensibility and stable deployment in open environments.
motivation: Quadrupeds are highly mobile platforms for deploying general-purpose embodied agents, but end-to-end models are hard to interpret, extend and deploy reliably. A hierarchical, modular design with an LLM planner over well-defined tool interfaces can avoid task-specific training and allow plug-and-play upgrades.
key_idea: An LLM task planner maps natural-language (voice) instructions to structured calls over a Tool Factory of modular executable capabilities (speech, LiDAR navigation, embodied QA) on a quadruped, with feedback-driven replanning and a distributed robot/server deployment.
insight: The paper is a system description and gives no ablations or experiments, so it offers no empirical insight. Its claim is that hierarchical decoupling (LLM planning over standardized module interfaces) improves interpretability, extensibility and deployment stability compared with end-to-end models. This claim is not quantitatively validated.
method: LLM Task Planner: a single LLM selects modules from structured descriptions (function, input parameters, applicable conditions, constraints), binds parameters to produce a structured plan, and uses historical plans and execution feedback for context and replanning.
Tool Factory: standardized-interface executable modules covering speech interaction, autonomous navigation and embodied question answering.
Speech interaction: ASR + TTS with an LLM for dialogue understanding and response, optionally with a knowledge base, voiceprint recognition and dialogue memory.

Autonomous navigation: fuses LiDAR, GNSS and IMU for global pose, builds a local obstacle-aware grid map from LiDAR point clouds, plans with A*, and updates map and path online without a pre-built map.

Embodied QA: after reaching the target, the robot rotates to scan, captures multi-view RGB, Qwen3-VL-Flash produces scene descriptions, and an LLM fuses them with the question and viewing angles to answer.

Workflow/infrastructure: the planner invokes modules synchronously and receives asynchronous feedback over a LAN. Unmatched requests fall back to open-ended dialogue via TTS. Heavy inference runs on a server while the robot keeps lightweight perception, control and transmission.

setting.backbone: Unspecified LLM planner (frozen) + Qwen3-VL-Flash (frozen) for scene description
setting.observation: Speech, multi-view RGB (rotational scan), LiDAR point clouds, GNSS, IMU
setting.action_space: High-level module/tool calls; navigation via A* paths on a local grid map executed by the quadruped controller

numbers_note: No quantitative experiments or results reported; system/demo paper (supplementary video only).
results: No quantitative results are reported. The paper presents a working reference implementation of a voice-driven, LLM-planned quadruped assistant with navigation and embodied QA, demonstrated in a supplementary video.
limitations: No quantitative evaluation, benchmarks, baselines or ablations, so claims about stability and extensibility are unsupported.
Depends on network connectivity to a server and on external LLM/VLM services; the LLM planner is unspecified and its failure or latency is not analyzed.
Embodied QA relies on a rotational scan and a single-shot captioning VLM, and navigation is only geometric (LiDAR/A*) with no semantic or instruction-grounded navigation.
